channel.title: The Western Producer - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Western Producer (producer.com)

item.title: U.S. to seek more foreign tariff cuts, CUSMA improvements in 2026
item.description: The U.S. Trade Representative’s office said on Monday it will seek further reductions in foreign tariffs and non-tariff barriers this year, enforce its “reciprocal” trade deals and consider launching new unfair trade practices investigations.

item.title: Beef certification program launches incentive
item.description: Beef producers who are Canadian Roundtable for Sustainable Beef certified will recieve $400 in October 2026 as part of the recently launched CRSB Certified Producer Incentive.

item.title: OPINION: Mark Carney’s visit to India hits the reset button on the Canada–India relationship
item.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney’s visit to India marks the most consequential step in years to rebuild Canada–India relations after the diplomatic rupture in 2023 over allegations linking Indian agents to the killing of a Canadian Sikh activist.

item.title: Soybean oil prices expected to rise in 2026-27
item.description: SASKATOON — The outlook for grains and oilseeds in 2026-27 is pretty blah, with one notable exception. The demand for U.S. soybean oil is expected to be voracious, said Bryn Swearingen, agricultural economist with the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Economic Research Service. She told delegates attending the USDA’s 102nd annual Agricultural Outlook Forum that the […] Read more

item.title: Canada, India team up on new pulse protein centre
item.description: Saskatchewan announced in a press release on March 3, 2026 it will team up with India on a proposed new pulse protein centre of excellence north of New Delhi.

item.title: Canadian Pacific Kansas City sees record February grain movement
item.description: Canadian Pacific Kansas City hit a new record for February movement of Canadian grain and grain products, moving 2.232 million tonnes in February 2026, the company reported on March 3.

item.title: Loblaw misses revenue estimate
item.description: Canadian retailer Loblaw says it has missed analysts’ estimates for fourth-quarter revenue, signalling consumers are turning cautious and more discerning.

item.title: CUSMA: a guide to the review and what it means for the agriculture sector
item.description: The upcoming Canada-Unites States-Mexico Agreement (CUSMA) review could set the tone for the future of Canadian agri-food trade. Here’s everything you need to know about CUSMA, the upcoming review process and what it could mean for the agriculture sector.

item.title: No way to segregate gene edited pigs Canadian Pork Council says as groups call for labeling
item.description: Canadian Pork Council says it supports bids to get public acceptance for pigs gene edited for resistance to PRRS as some consumer and agriculture groups call for mandatory labelling.

item.title: More canola, spring wheat likely to be seeded this spring
item.description: As spring planting approaches, farmers are busy planning which crops to seed this year and how much. With that, market thoughts have turned toward planted area projections, as Statistics Canada is set to issue its report on Thursday.
